newsitem.title: USA: Export data/deliveries seen stalling Aug soy rise.
newsitem.headline: Export data/deliveries seen stalling Aug soy rise.

text.p: A much lower-than-expected export tally for soybeans during the week ended August 7 plus the first posting of deliveries on the August CBOT soy contract were expected to stall a rise in the price of the August, traders said.
"That (the delivery posting) and the export sales will calm the August," a trader said.
CBOT August soybean futures closed 35-1/4 cents per bushel higher at $7.79 per bushel on Wednesday.

There were 40,000 bushels of soybeans posted Thursday for delivery on the August contract and all of the soy was listed by the Cargill Investor Services house account, according to the CBOT. There were scattered stoppers.

USDA Thursday said the net export sales of U.S. soybeans during the week ended August 7 totalled a minus 11,600 tonnes for old crop soybeans, well below expectations for 50,000 to 100,000 tonnes. Net sales of new crop soybeans totalled 198,800 tonnes, below expectatons for 300,000 to 350,000 tonnes.
CBOT soybean futures Thursday were called to open two to five cents per bushel lower on bearish input from Midwest weather, the USDA export report and on the delivery posting.
